records.notes: Civil writ petition under Article 226 challenging BIFR's registration of respondent's reference under SICA as a sick undertaking. Division Bench held that petitioner's contention that repeated references were barred had no absolute application where subsequent references were based on audited balance sheets, noted BIFR was yet to apply mind on net worth, and dismissed the writ petition on substantive merits. Interlocutory CM No. 4306/2016 for interim relief was consequentially dismissed as infructuous. Respondent company succeeded in defeating the challenge to the BIFR reference; successful party is respondent under Section 5 Row 124 of guidelines.

records.notes: Government Appeal under Section 378(3) CrPC by the State of U.P. challenging trial court judgment acquitting accused Santosh Kumar of charges under Sections 8/20 of NDPS Act. records.notes: Statutory appeal under Section 130E(b) of the Customs Act, 1962 from CEGAT order upholding confiscation, differential duty, and penalties under Sections 111(d), 111(m), 112, and 28 against appellant importers for fraudulent misdeclaration and gross undervaluation of imported safety equipment. Supreme Court held fraud unravels all, affirmed CEGAT findings as irreversible, held the appeals were sans merit, and dismissed them. [AUDIT NOTE Feature 4.16.1/4.16.2]: Original proposal was state_prosecution. However, successful party is the Commissioner of Customs (Import), Mumbai, an administrative/statutory revenue authority in a customs tariff and penalty appeal. Under Section 5 of the annotation guidelines, state_prosecution is strictly restricted to criminal prosecution and bail proceedings. Equating a revenue authority with criminal prosecution is unsupported by the taxonomy without expanding it. Per reviewer instructions, marked 'unresolved' to exclude from Model B substantive training while retaining Model A 'appeal_dismissed' (merits).

records.notes: Civil Appeal No. 1009 of 2006 under Article 136 against High Court order restraining financier from taking repossession of vehicle under hire-purchase agreement. Supreme Court held that financier's contractual right to repossession upon borrower default cannot be varied or restricted by judicial guidelines in suits for injunction, set aside the lower court order, and allowed the appeal on substantive merits. [AUDIT NOTE Feature 4.16.1/4.16.2]: Original proposal was petitioner. However, the successful party is The Managing Director, Orix Auto Finance (India) Ltd., who was defendant in the trial court and appellant before the Supreme Court. The annotation guidelines define petitioner specifically as the initiating party in high court writ or supervisory petitions, not as a civil appellant reversing an injunction. Mapping a successful appellant to petitioner creates label conflation. Marked 'unresolved' per reviewer instructions to avoid invalid class conflation, while retaining Model A 'appeal_allowed' (merits).
